items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: And anyway, I joined the band, Ernie Fields' band.

ctx.x: and he was giving me some fatherly advice, you know. And anyway, I joined the band, Ernie Fields' band. And we got to Pensacola, Florida; we played a dance in Pensacola. Our next stop was Monroe, Louisiana. [LAUGHS] Our next stop was Tulsa, Oklahoma! I'm gettin' farther and farther' away from New York, right...! [LAUGHS] So I stayed out there with them, and I began to get attached to the guys, you know, and be like a part of the band, and so you get sentimental, you know... So I ended up staying there with him.

And he had a very, very fine vocalist with this band, Melvin Moore. Great singer. Sing anything. In fact, he was really carrying the band until I got there and helped him carry it. Because when I went, I was playing the lead and most of the solos. In that original reed section, they had John White on one alto, and had... The baritone player was named Sy. And the tenor players were named Lucky... Warren Lucky was one of the tenor player's names; he was from Dallas, Texas -- good saxophone player. And the other…

items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: I sent back later and got Jack and Teddy Edwards, and Teddy Edwards turned out just very sensational.

ctx.x: and also he played piano, and so I talked with Jack and he was for it. I think it was in Jackson, Mississippi but they were originally out of Laurel, Mississippi and talked around, so you know how some of these guys are, I don't like to get into it, but like that buddy, you got to hire one with the other, but at the same time, I went to this little gig that they were playing, and I tell you the truth, I was just carried away with Teddy Edwards and so, they didn't have to influence me much about getting Teddy when…

I kind of played hard to get but I was glad to say yeah and I sent back later and got Jack and Teddy Edwards, and Teddy Edwards turned out just very sensational. I turned the reed section over to him and he worked with the guys. He was a nice musician; he could work with the brass men, but he meant a lot to my reed section.
